verses.english: The Simile of the Tree Trunk (2nd)

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kimilāyaṁ viharati gaṅgāya nadiyā tīre.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kimibilā on the bank of the Ganges river.

verses.pali: Addasā kho bhagavā mahantaṁ dārukkhandhaṁ gaṅgāya nadiyā sotena vuyhamānaṁ.
verses.english: Seeing a large tree trunk being carried along by the current,

verses.pali: “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, amuṁ mahantaṁ dārukkhandhaṁ gaṅgāya nadiyā sotena vuyhamānan”ti?
verses.english: “Mendicants, do you see that large tree trunk being carried along by the current of the Ganges river?”

verses.pali: evaṁ vutte, āyasmā kimilo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When this was said, Venerable Kimbila said to the Buddha:

“But sir, what’s the near shore and what’s the far shore? What’s sinking in the middle? What’s getting stranded on high ground? What’s getting taken by humans or non-humans? What’s getting caught up in a whirlpool? And what’s rotting away?” …

verses.pali: Idha, kimila, bhikkhu aññataraṁ saṅkiliṭṭhaṁ āpattiṁ āpanno hoti yathārūpāya āpattiyā na vuṭṭhānaṁ paññāyati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant has committed the kind of corrupt offense for which no rehabilitation is possible.
